images.title: Reading a fraction to mark
images.purpose: Show how to read any fraction as a marking instruction: the bottom number says how many equal parts to cut, the top number says how many parts to count from 0.
images.composition: A large sample fraction on the left with two short pointer lines, and one number line on the right with a single marked point, all well spaced.
images.exact_structure: Left: the fraction 3/5 written large, the 3 in amber #E69F00 and the 5 in teal #0072B2. Two thin grey #6B7280 pointer lines run from it to two short notes. Right: a grey number line from 0 to 1 with exactly 6 evenly spaced ticks making 5 equal parts; the 5 parts are lightly banded teal and white. A reddish purple #CC79A7 point sits on the 3rd tick after 0. Exactly 1 fraction, 1 number line, 1 point.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a point placed anywhere other than the 3rd tick after 0
images.takeaway: Cut by the bottom number, count by the top number, starting from 0.
images.description: A sample fraction 3/5 split into two instructions, cut into 5 equal parts and count 3 parts from 0, next to a number line where the point 3/5 is marked.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the teal 5 and the amber 3 and say what each one tells them to do.

image_decisions.why: A sample fraction turned into cut and count steps gives the student a method for any fraction they choose.
